title: After the midterms, is the AI industry in for a rough two years?
slides: Will AI's Washington honeymoon end after midterms?
Lawmakers return with new tech oversight bills
But few actually target AI algorithms directly
Companies must now document model risks for audits
Start tracking every compliance requirement this quarter
thread_text:
1. Washington's AI Honeymoon May Be Over

Lawmakers return with new tech oversight bills, but few actually target AI algorithms directly. Companies now must document model risks for audits — starting this quarter.

2. Oversight Bills Miss The Algorithm

Most proposals focus on transparency and reporting, not on how AI models make decisions. That gap leaves the core technology largely unregulated.

3. Audits Are Now Your Problem

Firms must document model risks for compliance reviews. If you build or deploy AI, the paperwork starts now — not next year.

4. Compliance Deadline This Quarter

Tracking every requirement is no longer optional. Miss it, and you risk audits, fines, or stalled deployments.

5. Audit Your Own AI Today

Pick one model you use and write down its risks in plain language. If you can't, you're already behind this quarter.
